item.title: Tributes to Gloria Steinem are flooding in, from Hollywood to Capitol Hill
item.description: Women in politics and pop culture are paying tribute to Gloria Steinem after her death at 92. Many called her not only an inspiration but a friend.

item.title: Later in life, Gloria Steinem found herself free of the 'demands of gender'
item.description: In 2015, the trailblazing feminist told Fresh Air she that had entered a new phase in life, one in which "you can do what you want." Steinem died Sept. 2 at the age of 92.

item.title: See inequity through the eyes of a 'tee girl' at a fancy resort in 'Filipiñana'
item.description: Seventeen-year-old Isabel tees up balls for golfers in a lush luxury oasis in Manila. It's the feature film debut of writer and director Rafael Manuel, and every shot of Filipiñana churns with life.

item.title: 'The Uprising' director Paul Greengrass on the 'great rage' of history -- and today
item.description: Greengrass' latest film is set in 1381 England and centers on a farmer who leads an army against the king. His previous films include the Jason Bourne movies, United 93 and Captain Phillips.

item.title: An epic train chase is turning 100 — and Buster Keaton fans are celebrating
item.description: 100 years ago, silent film star Buster Keaton filmed The General in Cottage Grove, Ore. Fans are gathering there to celebrate the making of an epic early film.

item.title: Understanding the tech giants' oversized influence in American schools
item.description: Big tech companies like Apple and Microsoft use devices, training and conferences for teachers and students to embed in schools. The New York Times' Natasha Singer discusses the impact in Coding Kids.

item.title: Greetings from the Royal Pavilion, a stunning reminder of India in southern England
item.description: Looking up at this 18th century building, it became clear the British didn't only bring their architectural style to India. They also took some of India's style home.

item.title: Milwaukee's Veggie Chop Shop uses farmers' excess produce to feed those in need
item.description: A program called the Veggie Chop Shop enlists volunteers to gather extra produce from farmers' markets that would otherwise go to waste. They then cook meals for people facing food insecurity.
